html:
The Kankuamo are one of the four Indigenous peoples of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, a mountain block on the Caribbean coast of Colombia, with the Kogi, the Arhuaco and the Wiwa. They live on the southeastern slopes, near Valledupar.

The four peoples see themselves as heirs of the Tairona and as guardians of the mountain. The Kankuamo were the most affected by Spanish and later Colombian settlement and lost their language. From the 1990s they revived their identity and got a reserve recognised. In the early 2000s many Kankuamo were killed in the armed conflict between guerrillas and paramilitaries.
